items.followUp: State the rules for writing the scientific name of an organism.

rubric.why: A binomial name has two parts: the genus name and the species name.
rubric.description: Identifies the two parts of a binomial name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both genus and species.

rubric.why: Scientific names follow conventions for capitalization and formatting.
rubric.description: States a convention for writing scientific names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the capitalization convention or the italics/underlining convention.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature gives each organism a two-word scientific name: the genus name followed by the species name.
The genus name begins with a capital letter, while the species name begins with a lowercase letter; the names are written in italics or underlined separately when handwritten.

items.followUp: What is the function of sclerenchyma tissue?

rubric.why: Collenchyma consists of living cells whose walls are unevenly thickened at the corners.
rubric.description: Describes the cells and their characteristic wall thickening.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying living cells and uneven thickening at the corners.

rubric.why: Collenchyma supports young plant parts while allowing them to bend without breaking.
rubric.description: States the tissue’s role in young plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for support and flexibility in young parts.

modelAnswer: Collenchyma is a simple permanent tissue made of living, elongated cells with walls unevenly thickened at the corners.
It provides support and flexibility to young parts of the plant, such as stems and leaves.

items.followUp: What are enzymes, and how do they affect chemical reactions in living organisms?

rubric.why: Biocatalysts are biological catalysts, usually enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as biological catalysts or enzymes that act as catalysts.

rubric.why: Biocatalysts speed up chemical reactions and are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.
rubric.description: States their effect on reactions and that they are not consumed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they speed up reactions and are not used up.

modelAnswer: Biocatalysts are biological catalysts, usually enzymes, that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms.
They are not used up or permanently changed in the reactions they catalyse.

items.followUp: Why is ATP called the energy currency of the cell?

rubric.why: ATP stores energy in the bonds between its phosphate groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stored energy with ATP’s phosphate bonds or groups.

rubric.why: ATP releases energy that cells use to carry out their activities.
rubric.description: Explains how ATP provides energy to the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP supplies or releases energy for cellular activities.

modelAnswer: ATP stores energy in the bonds between its phosphate groups.
When energy is needed, ATP releases it for cellular activities; therefore, ATP acts as the cell’s energy currency.

items.followUp: State one role of magnesium in plant life.

rubric.why: Potassium activates several enzymes in plants.
rubric.description: States potassium’s role in enzyme activation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that potassium activates enzymes.

rubric.why: Potassium helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata.
rubric.description: States potassium’s role in stomatal regulation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking potassium with regulation of stomata.

modelAnswer: Potassium activates several enzymes in plants.
It also helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

items.followUp: What is compost, and how does it improve soil?

rubric.why: Organic fertilizer is a natural material from plant or animal matter that is added to soil to improve fertility.
rubric.description: Defines organic fertilizer by its source and purpose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its plant or animal origin and its use as a fertilizer to improve soil.

rubric.why: Farmyard manure and compost are examples of organic fertilizers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: An organic fertilizer is a natural material made from plant or animal matter and added to soil to improve its fertility.
